data.name: Dark Fall: Lost Souls
data.detailed_description:
Some say the old train station and hotel are a 'haunted hotspot', hidden away in the woods, forgotten by some, feared by others. The old hallways and train platforms echo with the ghosts of many eras, all trapped within the very fabric of the place, each hoping for salvation. The dusty old rooms seem possessed, exhibiting 'time slips' as the past becomes the present. You must tread very carefully, or you too many join the Lost Souls forever. So, why are you here?

Amy Haven went missing 5 Years ago. On the anniversary of the child's disappearance you, the Police Inspector who failed to find her, has returned to the Train Station and Hotel one last time. As you attempt to solve the mystery of Amy's disappearance you must face the horrors of your past. Someone, or something, does not want you to solve the mystery, that much is clear. Never turn your back on the darkness....for something hides there; something evil, unknowable and hungry.

Key features:

  • A stand-alone Dark Fall horror adventure.
  • Explore a derelict train station & hotel, abandoned since World War 2.
  • Experience 'timeslips' as the past becomes the present.
  • Communicate with ghosts, the Lost Souls, and attempt to free them from purgatory.
  • A hauntingly creepy score, to chill, alarm and horrify.
  • Explore the memories of the dead, in their own ‘nightmares’.
  • Discover the true identity, and power behind, the Dark Fall itself.
  • Play twisted 'Party Games' including Blind Man's Buff and Statues.
  • Solve a modern urban mystery, 'What Happened To Amy Haven?'
  • Use a Ouijaboard to meet and communicate with ghosts.
  • Survive the night in a realistic, abandoned location full of danger!

reviews.review:
Dark Fall: Lost Souls is an atmospheric psychological horror adventure that successfully combines supernatural investigation, disturbing storytelling, and traditional point-and-click gameplay into an unsettling journey through a forgotten location. Developed and published by Darkling Room, the game emphasizes mystery, exploration, and psychological tension rather than conventional action. Its greatest strength lies in creating an environment where every abandoned room, mysterious sound, and unexplained occurrence contributes to an overwhelming sense of dread. Players who appreciate slow-burning horror and intellectually engaging mysteries will find plenty to appreciate in this haunting experience.

The narrative follows a police inspector returning to an abandoned railway station and hotel five years after the mysterious disappearance of a young girl named Amy Haven. Having failed to solve the original case, the inspector remains burdened by guilt and unresolved questions. His determination to uncover the truth leads him into a supernatural nightmare where personal memories, disturbing revelations, and malevolent forces become increasingly intertwined. The story effectively explores obsession, regret, and the consequences of unresolved trauma, giving the investigation emotional significance beyond its paranormal elements.

The abandoned railway station and adjoining hotel provide an exceptionally fitting setting for the unfolding mystery. Deserted platforms, decaying corridors, neglected rooms, and unsettling environmental details establish an atmosphere of isolation and forgotten tragedy. The location feels like a character itself, with its mysterious history gradually emerging through exploration. The game's environmental storytelling encourages players to examine their surroundings carefully, transforming seemingly ordinary objects and locations into potential pieces of a much larger supernatural puzzle.

One particularly fascinating element involves supernatural time slips that temporarily blur the distinction between different historical periods. These occurrences suggest that the location exists outside conventional boundaries of time, allowing fragments of the past to intrude upon the present. This concept strengthens the narrative while introducing intriguing possibilities for exploration and discovery. The presence of spirits trapped between different eras further reinforces the unsettling idea that the station has become a prison for restless souls.

Gameplay primarily revolves around first-person exploration, environmental interaction, and puzzle-solving. Players investigate abandoned locations, collect information, examine suspicious objects, and gradually connect clues to advance the mystery. Progress depends heavily on observation, patience, and logical thinking rather than reflexes or combat abilities. The traditional adventure structure provides satisfying challenges for enthusiasts of investigative games, although certain puzzles can feel obscure, occasionally requiring experimentation or revisiting previously explored areas.

Communication with supernatural entities represents another distinctive aspect of the experience. Using a Ouija board to contact restless spirits introduces an intriguing investigative mechanic, allowing players to uncover information concealed beyond the physical world. Exploring the memories and nightmares of deceased individuals expands the narrative while revealing the suffering that binds these souls to the location. The possibility of helping them escape their supernatural imprisonment adds emotional depth to encounters that might otherwise function purely as frightening distractions.

The inclusion of sinister childhood party games, particularly Blind Man's Buff and Statues, introduces an imaginative form of psychological horror. Activities normally associated with innocence and entertainment become threatening when transformed into supernatural challenges. These encounters provide variety while reinforcing the game's recurring themes of childhood vulnerability, corrupted memories, and unseen danger. Their unsettling presentation helps distinguish the adventure from more conventional ghost stories.

Audio design contributes significantly to the overall experience. Haunting music, unsettling environmental noises, and carefully timed moments of silence establish a persistent feeling of uncertainty. The soundtrack complements the abandoned surroundings without overwhelming the atmosphere, allowing subtle auditory details to create anticipation. The resulting tension frequently emerges from what players suspect might happen rather than from constant visual threats.

Visually, the game employs realistic environments, oppressive lighting, and deteriorating architectural details to establish its disturbing identity. Although its graphics and interface reveal their age, the artistic direction remains effective in communicating isolation and supernatural unease. The relatively static presentation and traditional navigation mechanics may feel restrictive compared with contemporary horror adventures, but they also encourage deliberate observation and careful investigation.

Despite its atmospheric strengths, the experience is not without shortcomings. The pacing occasionally becomes sluggish, particularly when players encounter unclear objectives or difficult puzzles. Navigation can feel cumbersome, and the absence of modern convenience features may frustrate newcomers. Additionally, its emphasis on exploration and psychological storytelling means players expecting frequent combat or continuous action may find the experience insufficiently dynamic. Nevertheless, these limitations are easier to overlook when approached as a traditional investigative horror adventure.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, the game currently has an Unknown compatibility classification, meaning it has not received an official Verified or Playable designation from Valve. Its Windows-oriented requirements and mouse-based interaction system introduce potential challenges for handheld operation. Proton compatibility and customized trackpad controls may offer possible solutions, but reliable functionality cannot be guaranteed without testing. Consequently, Steam Deck users should approach the game cautiously rather than assuming complete compatibility.

Overall, Dark Fall: Lost Souls delivers an engaging supernatural mystery supported by unsettling environments, thoughtful investigative mechanics, and psychologically disturbing storytelling. Its exploration of guilt, paranormal imprisonment, and forgotten tragedies creates a memorable atmosphere that remains its defining achievement. Although dated controls, occasionally frustrating puzzles, and deliberate pacing limit its accessibility, the experience remains particularly worthwhile for players who appreciate classic adventure games and atmospheric ghost stories.

A compelling psychological horror adventure featuring excellent atmosphere, intriguing supernatural mysteries, and rewarding exploration, somewhat hindered by aging mechanics and occasional puzzle frustrations.

Rating: 7/10
